chapter: Ch 4: Presentation and Disclosures Based Accounting Standards
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Scope, Objective and Key Definitions of AS 25
explain: AS 25 does not mandate which entities must publish interim reports, nor how often or how quickly.
If an enterprise prepares and presents an interim financial report, it must fully comply with AS 25.
An interim period is any financial reporting period shorter than a full financial year.
A shorter initial operating period in the first year of a business is treated as its full year, not an interim period.
An interim financial report can contain either a complete set or a condensed set of financial statements.

flow.title: Scope Applicability Test
steps: Check if interim financial report is presented
Check if period is shorter than financial year
Exclude initial short operating first year
Apply AS 25 standards and rules

topics.example: A company incorporated in July closes its first financial year in March (9 months); this 9-month period is its first annual year, not an interim period.
remember: Interim period is any reporting period shorter than a full financial year.
AS 25 sets content and measurement principles but does not force entities to report.
mistakes: Assuming AS 25 mandates quarterly reporting for all companies (the mandate comes from regulatory bodies like SEBI, not AS 25).

quiz.q: Does AS 25 mandate which enterprises must prepare interim financial reports?
o: Yes, for all corporate entities
Yes, only for listed companies
No, it does not mandate reporting
Yes, for statutory corporations
quiz.why: AS 25 prescribes standard requirements if a report is prepared, but does not specify who must prepare one.

quiz.q: In the first year of business operations, an entity operates for 8 months before year-end. Is this an interim period under AS 25?
o: Yes, because it is under 12 months
No, a shorter first annual period is not an interim period
Yes, provided the entity is listed
Only if permitted by tax regulators
quiz.why: During the first year of operations, a shorter reporting period is considered a full financial year, not an interim period.

topics.title: Content, Form, and Structure of Interim Statements
explain: An interim financial report requires at minimum a set of condensed financial statements.
Entities may elect to present a complete set conforming to full annual accounting standard rules.
Condensed statements focus on new events and activities to avoid duplicating prior annual disclosures.
Condensed statements must include at minimum all headings and sub-headings from the latest annual statements.
Basic and Diluted EPS as per AS 20 must be presented on the face of the P&L statement (complete or condensed).

flow.title: Form and Content Selection
steps: Choose complete or condensed interim format
Include all recent annual headings and sub-headings
Add selected explanatory notes for new events
Present Basic and Diluted EPS on P&L face

topics.example: If the annual Balance Sheet presents 'Property, Plant and Equipment' as a sub-heading, the condensed interim Balance Sheet must also display this sub-heading.
remember: Minimum requirement = Condensed financial statements + Selected explanatory notes.
Basic and Diluted EPS must appear on the face of the P&L statement.
mistakes: Omitting Basic or Diluted EPS from condensed interim P&L statements.

quiz.q: What is the minimum component of an Interim Financial Report under AS 25?
o: Full annual report with audit notes
Condensed financial statements and selected notes
Only Balance Sheet and Profit and Loss statement
Directors report and Cash Flow statement
quiz.why: AS 25 requires at a minimum a set of condensed financial statements and selected explanatory notes.

quiz.q: How must Earnings Per Share (EPS) be reported in condensed interim financial statements?
o: It is optional in condensed statements
Only disclosed inside explanatory notes
Basic and Diluted EPS presented on P&L face
Only annual EPS needs to be calculated
quiz.why: Both basic and diluted EPS must be presented on the face of the Statement of Profit and Loss as per AS 20.

topics.title: Selected Explanatory Notes and Materiality Criteria
explain: Selected notes update the latest annual disclosures with material events and changes during the interim period.
Notes must cover accounting policy changes, seasonality, unusual items, estimate changes, debt/equity changes, dividends, segment results, and contingent liabilities.
Explanatory note information should normally be reported on a financial year-to-date basis.
Materiality is assessed in relation to the interim period financial data, not the full annual figures.
Interim measurements rely on estimates to a greater extent than annual measurements.

flow.title: Explanatory Notes Preparation
steps: Identify events since last annual balance sheet
Evaluate materiality against interim period figures
Prepare explanatory notes on year-to-date basis
Disclose changes in policies, estimates, or structure

topics.example: An extraordinary loss of ₹5 lakhs might be immaterial for an annual profit of ₹500 lakhs, but material for a quarterly profit of ₹10 lakhs, requiring disclosure.
remember: Materiality is evaluated against interim period figures, not annual figures.
Explanatory notes are primarily prepared on a financial year-to-date basis.
mistakes: Evaluating the materiality of an interim event using annual income, resulting in the omission of material interim notes.

quiz.q: On what basis is materiality assessed for interim financial reporting purposes?
o: In relation to full annual financial data
In relation to interim period financial data
Fixed absolute amount threshold of ₹10 lakhs
Based entirely on auditor discretion
quiz.why: Under AS 25, materiality for recognition and disclosure decisions is evaluated relative to interim period financial data.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a mandatory selected explanatory note under AS 25?
o: Commentary on seasonality of interim operations
Segment revenue and segment result under AS 17
Complete nominal list of all shareholders
Material changes in contingent liabilities
quiz.why: A nominal list of shareholders is not part of the selected explanatory notes required by AS 25.

topics.title: Required Presentation Periods and Annual Disclosures
explain: Balance Sheet: End of current interim period vs. End of immediately preceding financial year.
P&L Statement: Current interim period and year-to-date vs. Comparable interim period and year-to-date of preceding financial year.
Cash Flow Statement: Cumulative current year-to-date vs. Comparable year-to-date of preceding financial year.
Transitional provision: Comparative P&L and Cash Flow for prior year are not required on first adoption of AS 25.
If an estimate changes significantly in the final interim period without a separate report, it must be disclosed in the annual financial statements.

flow.title: Interim Reporting Period Mapping
steps: Compare interim Balance Sheet with prior year-end
Compare interim P&L with prior same quarter & YTD
Compare Cash Flow YTD with prior year YTD
Disclose un-reported final quarter estimate changes annually

topics.example: For Q3 ended 31st December 20X1 (FY 20X1-X2), the Balance Sheet comparative date is 31st March 20X1 (preceding year-end).
remember: Balance Sheet comparative is always the end of the preceding financial year.
Transitional rules exempt prior comparative P&L and Cash Flow on first-time adoption.
mistakes: Comparing the interim Balance Sheet with the same quarter of the previous year instead of the previous year-end date.

quiz.q: What is the comparative period for an interim Balance Sheet as at 31st December 20X1?
o: As at 31st December 20X0
As at 31st March 20X1
As at 30th September 20X1
As at 1st April 20X1
quiz.why: The comparative period for an interim balance sheet is the end of the immediately preceding financial year.

quiz.q: If an accounting estimate changes drastically in Q4 but no standalone Q4 interim report is published, where is it disclosed?
o: No disclosure is needed
In the next year's Q1 report
In a note to the annual financial statements
In a public press announcement only
quiz.why: Significant changes in estimates in the final interim period without a separate report must be disclosed in the annual notes.

topics.title: Recognition & Measurement Principles
explain: An enterprise must apply the same accounting policies in interim reports as in annual statements.
Seasonal, cyclical, or occasional revenues (e.g., dividends, grants, seasonal sales) must be recognized when earned—never anticipated or deferred.
Costs incurred unevenly during the year are anticipated/deferred ONLY IF it is appropriate to do so at financial year-end.
Costs not meeting asset criteria at interim date cannot be deferred as assets to smooth quarterly earnings.
Income tax expense is recognized in each interim period based on the best estimate of the weighted average annual effective tax rate.
Impairment losses recognized in Q1 can be reversed in Q2 if recoverable amounts increase due to favorable indicators.
For Clause 41 listing results, only AS 25 recognition and measurement principles apply.

flow.title: Interim Tax Expense Calculation
steps: Estimate total annual income and tax liability
Compute weighted average annual effective tax rate
Determine actual interim income for the period
Multiply interim income by weighted average rate

topics.example: If estimated annual income is ₹10 lakhs and estimated annual tax is ₹3.5 lakhs (35% weighted rate), Q1 profit of ₹75,000 gets a tax expense of ₹26,250 (35% of ₹75,000).
remember: Seasonal revenues are recognized when incurred/earned; deferring uniform costs to match seasonal sales is prohibited.
Interim Tax Expense = Interim Income × Estimated Weighted Average Annual Tax Rate.
mistakes: Deferring routine Q1 advertisement expenses to Q3 on the logic that Q3 generates 60% of total annual sales.

quiz.q: How should seasonal revenue earned in Q3 be recognized under AS 25?
o: Spread evenly across all four quarters
Deferred to Q4
Recognized entirely in Q3 when it occurs
Anticipated starting from Q1
quiz.why: Revenues received seasonally or occasionally must not be anticipated or deferred; they are recognized when they occur.

quiz.q: How is income tax expense calculated for an interim reporting period under AS 25?
o: Actual tax paid during that specific quarter
Interim profit multiplied by estimated weighted average annual tax rate
Flat rate of 30% applied to quarterly profit
Tax is recognized entirely in the 4th quarter
quiz.why: Tax expense is measured using the best estimate of the weighted average annual effective income tax rate applied to interim profit.
